findings.quoteLive: CLAUDE-G01H-V5-MF1 and CLAUDE-G01H-V5-SF1 land in this v6.
findings.quoteLiveFullNode: Predecessor. Unmoved. Lands CLAUDE-G01H-V4-MF1 and CLAUDE-G01H-V4-MF2. Dual not 0/0. CLAUDE-G01H-V5-MF1 and CLAUDE-G01H-V5-SF1 land in this v6. Not recordable as a current occupancy remasurement. Not this artifact's version number.
findings.why: The subject declares at failsIf[25] (1-indexed; 0-indexed 24) that it fails if 'speaker labels say This v1, This v2, This v3, This v4, This v5, or This v6 for this subject'. The subject is v7: top-level artifact is 'harness.DR-G01.core-download.v7' and version is 7. The quoted sentence says the two V5 findings land in 'this v6'. In this document 'this vN' is the subject-speaker construction and nothing else: it occurs twelve times outside the failsIf roster and in every one of those twelve it denotes the current artifact and reads 'this v7'. One occurrence, and only one, reads 'this v6'. By the subject's own declared invariant that occurrence is fatal.
findings.whyNotMerelyCosmetic: The sentence is a landing-locus statement, not decoration. It answers the question 'where did CLAUDE-G01H-V5-MF1 and CLAUDE-G01H-V5-SF1 land?' with 'this v6' -- that is, with the document the reader is holding. The document the reader is holding is v7. A reader reconstructing the remediation chain from this file is told that the current occupancy remasurement is v6 and that the V5 findings land in it. Both halves are false: v6 is frozen, was dual REJECT, and is listed by this same subject at proposedLaterWork[9] as 'Frozen v6 remains a historical occupancy that was dual REJECT. Do not record v6 as current.' The node therefore contradicts, inside one basedOn object, the currency roster the same file publishes. It also carries a secondary and weaker trip of failsIf[8], 'v1, v2, v3, v4, v5, or v6 is recorded as a current occupancy remasurement', by labelling the live occupancy remasurement 'v6'; this reviewer anchors the finding on failsIf[25], which is unambiguous, and does not rest it on failsIf[8].
findings.steelmanConsidered: The strongest defence available to the subject is that 'this v6' parses as 'the v6 of this lineage' rather than 'this document, which is v6'. Under that reading the sentence is factually true: CLAUDE-G01H-V5-MF1 and CLAUDE-G01H-V5-SF1 did land in v6, and the finding would be a nitpick.
findings.steelmanRefuted: That defence fails on the author's own remediation vocabulary. CLAUDE-G01H-V6-MF2 required predecessorV4.role to stop saying 'lands in this v5'. The author's fix, verified by structural diff of v6 against v7, was to rewrite 'Lands CLAUDE-G01H-V4-MF1 and CLAUDE-G01H-V4-MF2 in this v5.' into 'CLAUDE-G01H-V4-MF1 and CLAUDE-G01H-V4-MF2 landed in this lineage at v5.' The author inserted the words 'in this lineage at' precisely to force the lineage reading, and simultaneously moved 'Lands' to the past tense 'landed'. That edit is a declaration by the author that bare 'in this vN' does NOT carry the lineage reading and is the defective form, and that 'in this lineage at vN' is the corrected form. predecessorV5.role retains the defective form verbatim, including the present-tense 'land' for a landing that is already frozen in the past. The subject cannot claim the lineage reading for predecessorV5.role while its own accepted fix for the identical construction one node earlier presupposes that the lineage reading is unavailable without the added words. The two nodes sit adjacent in the same basedOn object and now use two different conventions for the same relation.
findings.provenanceOfDefect: Structural diff of harness.DR-G01.core-download.v6.json against v7 shows the author performed a v6-to-v7 speaker sweep and updated 'This v6' to 'This v7' in eleven places: basedOn.namingV6.role, basedOn.cghsV4.role, basedOn.predecessorV1.role (both occurrences), basedOn.d173.role, basedOn.d230.role, namingStandingCarried, whatThisClosesNote, failsIf[2], and proposedLaterWork[1], [3], [4] and [5] (1-indexed). basedOn.predecessorV5.role is byte-identical between v6 and v7 and is the only node in the document still carrying a v6 speaker. In v6 that sentence was correct, because v6 was then the subject; the version bump is what made it stale. This is therefore a defect newly introduced by v7, not an unlanded prior finding, and it could not have been raised against v6.
findings.fix: In basedOn.predecessorV5.role, replace 'CLAUDE-G01H-V5-MF1 and CLAUDE-G01H-V5-SF1 land in this v6.' with the form the author already adopted at predecessorV4.role one node earlier: 'CLAUDE-G01H-V5-MF1 and CLAUDE-G01H-V5-SF1 landed in this lineage at v6.' This restores a single convention across predecessorV4.role and predecessorV5.role, removes the last v6 speaker, and preserves the true historical fact that those two findings landed in v6.
findings.classNote: To close the class rather than the instance, a successor should state the speaker rule once as an explicit discipline -- for example that no basedOn.* role may contain the token 'this v<N>' for any N other than the subject's own version -- so the invariant is mechanically checkable at authoring time instead of being re-swept by hand at every version bump. Three consecutive versions have now shipped a residue of this same sweep.

observationsNotFindings: basedOn.predecessorV6.role summarises the v6 dual REJECT as 'One shared class: leftover this-v5 speaker in predecessorV1.role (and predecessorV4.role).' That characterisation of the v6 findings is accurate as to those two nodes. It is not itself a finding. It is, however, the proximate cause of CLAUDE-G01H-V7-MF1: the author scoped the v7 sweep to the two nodes the v6 findings named instead of to every node carrying a version speaker, and predecessorV5.role fell outside that scope.

predecessorV5.role's opening 'Lands CLAUDE-G01H-V4-MF1 and CLAUDE-G01H-V4-MF2.' uses the present tense for a landing that is frozen in the past, but it carries no 'this vN' speaker and so does not trip failsIf[25]. It is tense drift only. Folding it into the same rewrite would be tidy but is not required to clear the MUST-FIX.

The subject's naming discipline correctly and repeatedly warns that naming v6, leftover-join v7 and G01 harness occupancy are unrelated lineages whose version numbers must not be read across. That discipline is sound and is what makes CLAUDE-G01H-V7-MF1 a real hazard rather than a typo: in a document that pins a naming v6 and a leftover-join v7 side by side, a stray 'this v6' is exactly the cross-lineage misread the document elsewhere works to prevent.
